newsitem.title: FRANCE: French firm SEP to switch motors for Ariane launch.
newsitem.headline: French firm SEP to switch motors for Ariane launch.

text.p: French engine maker SEP (Societe Europeenne de Propulsion) has decided to change the motor due to power the Ariane 5 rocket on its next launch, SEP chairman Roger Vignelles said on Saturday.
"We had a glitch and we've decided to switch the motor for flight 502," he told a news conference at the Paris air show.
Flight 502 will be the second Ariane 5 launch. The first Ariane 5 rocket exploded on its maiden voyage last June shortly after takeoff, but the motor was not believed to have been at fault.

Vignelles said a defect was spotted in a silver component during a test. The supplier who delivered the part used in the test motor also delivered the part for the motor slated for the mid-September launch.
SEP will still use the same type of motor, the Vulcain, but will use the engine slated for the following launch because the silver part in that engine is made by a different supplier.
"We think it's more prudent to use the motor slated for flight 503," a company official said.

An industry source said the switch, expected to take about 15 days, was likely to delay the launch but the companies involved were taking extra care after last year's disaster. The second Ariane 5 mission has already been delayed several times.
SEP is a subsidiary of state-owned aero-engine maker SNECMA.
